options.content:
**Oracle Enterprise Manager - Database & Host Performance**

Uses OEM repository queries from mgmt$metric_details, mgmt$metric_hourly, and mgmt$metric_daily tables.
OEM datasource is configured and user has SELECT on mgmt$ tables.

**Important:** Ensure the $TimePicker variable is set appropriately for the selected time range (Raw 1-day / Hourly 7-30 days / Daily 365 days).

panels.description: Percentage of total CPU capacity being used across application and database servers over time.

targets.rawQuery: SELECT from_tz(CAST(m.collection_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec, 'cpuusage_ps' AS metric, m.value AS value FROM mgmt$metric_details m, mgmt$target t WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type AND m.metric_name = 'instance_efficiency' AND m.metric_column = 'cpuusage_ps' AND m.collection_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE) AND m.collection_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE) ORDER BY time_sec ASC

panels.title: CPU Utilization (%)

panels.description: Amount of database time consumed per second showing overall database utilization.

panels.title: Buffer Cache Hit (%)

panels.description: FIXED: applies the 3-tier raw/hourly/daily repository query pattern (memory_usage / pctmemusage), matching the confirmed-working 'Total Memory Usage (MB)' panel's metric family.

targets.rawQuery:
SELECT
    from_tz(CAST(m.collection_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec,
    'pctmemusage' AS metric,
    m.value AS value
FROM mgmt$metric_details m, mgmt$target t
WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name
    AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type
    AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type
    AND m.metric_name = 'memory_usage'
    AND m.metric_column = 'pctmemusage'
    AND m.collection_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
    AND m.collection_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
ORDER BY time_sec ASC

SELECT
    from_tz(CAST(m.rollup_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec,
    'pctmemusage' AS metric,
    m.average AS value
FROM mgmt$metric_hourly m, mgmt$target t
WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name
    AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type
    AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type
    AND m.metric_name = 'memory_usage'
    AND m.metric_column = 'pctmemusage'
    AND m.rollup_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
    AND m.rollup_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
ORDER BY time_sec ASC

SELECT
    from_tz(CAST(m.rollup_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec,
    'pctmemusage' AS metric,
    m.average AS value
FROM mgmt$metric_daily m, mgmt$target t
WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name
    AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type
    AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type
    AND m.metric_name = 'memory_usage'
    AND m.metric_column = 'pctmemusage'
    AND m.rollup_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
    AND m.rollup_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
ORDER BY time_sec ASC

panels.title: Memory Usage (%)

panels.description: NOT FIXED: no confirmed metric_name/metric_column exists in either reference dashboard for disk latency. This may be a HOST-level metric (target_type='host') rather than a database-level one, which would explain why it returns nothing while this dashboard is locked to $oem_gf_target_type=oracle_database. Check Enterprise Manager under Target > Monitoring > All Metrics for the exact metric_name/metric_column before wiring this panel up, then apply the same raw/hourly/daily pattern used elsewhere on this dashboard. The query below is UNCHANGED from the original broken panel.

targets.rawQuery: SELECT from_tz(CAST(m.collection_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec, 'disk_latency' AS metric, m.value AS value FROM mgmt$metric_details m, mgmt$target t WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type AND m.metric_name = 'disk' AND m.metric_column = 'disk_latency' AND m.collection_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE) AND m.collection_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE) ORDER BY time_sec ASC

panels.title: Disk Latency (ms)

panels.description: FIXED: this is a live status snapshot, not a metric-history series. Replaced the mgmt$metric_details query (metric_name='availability'/metric_column='pct_available', which never populated) with the status-current view used in the working 'Single Instance Database Overview' dashboard, and swapped the panel type from gauge to stat with a status-code value mapping.

targets.rawQuery:
select 
    sysdate as time_sec,
    c.availability_status_code AS Status,
    c.availability_status as metric
FROM sysman.mgmt$availability_current c
WHERE c.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name
    AND c.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type

panels.title: Server Availability (%)

panels.description: FIXED: applies the 3-tier raw/hourly/daily repository query pattern to the same sysTimeModel metric family as the confirmed-working 'DB Time per Second' and 'SQL Execution Time per Second' panels.

targets.rawQuery:
SELECT

    'dbCpuTimePs' AS metric,

SELECT
    from_tz(CAST(m.rollup_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec,
    'dbCpuTimePs' AS metric,
    m.average AS value
FROM mgmt$metric_hourly m, mgmt$target t
WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name
    AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type
    AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type
    AND m.metric_name = 'sysTimeModel'
    AND m.metric_column = 'dbCpuTimePs'
    AND m.rollup_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
    AND m.rollup_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
ORDER BY time_sec ASC

SELECT
    from_tz(CAST(m.rollup_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP), t.timezone_region) AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time_sec,
    'dbCpuTimePs' AS metric,
    m.average AS value
FROM mgmt$metric_daily m, mgmt$target t
WHERE m.target_name = $oem_gf_target_name
    AND m.target_type = $oem_gf_target_type
    AND t.target_name = m.target_name AND t.target_type = m.target_type
    AND m.metric_name = 'sysTimeModel'
    AND m.metric_column = 'dbCpuTimePs'
    AND m.rollup_timestamp >= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__from:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
    AND m.rollup_timestamp <= CAST(TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ('${__to:date}') AT TIME ZONE t.timezone_region AS DATE)
ORDER BY time_sec ASC

panels.title: DB CPU Time (sec)

panels.description: NOT FIXED: this queries v$system_event directly, a live dynamic-performance view on the TARGET database. The oracle-emcc-datasource connects to the OEM REPOSITORY, which does not expose target v$ views, so this table cannot be reached this way regardless of syntax. Real fixes: (1) remove this panel, (2) build an OEM Metric Extension that snapshots wait events into mgmt$metric_details on a schedule and query that instead, or (3) add a second Grafana datasource pointed directly at the target database. The query below is UNCHANGED from the original broken panel.

targets.rawQuery: SELECT event, ROUND(time_waited_micro/1000000, 2) as wait_time_seconds FROM v$system_event WHERE wait_class != 'Idle' AND time_waited_micro > 0 ORDER BY time_waited_micro DESC FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY

panels.title: Top Wait Events

panels.description: NOT FIXED: this queries v$sql_monitor directly, a live dynamic-performance view on the TARGET database, unreachable from the OEM REPOSITORY datasource for the same reason as 'Top Wait Events' above. Real fixes: (1) remove this panel, (2) build an OEM Metric Extension that snapshots long-running SQL into mgmt$metric_details, or (3) add a second Grafana datasource pointed directly at the target database. The query below is UNCHANGED from the original broken panel.

targets.rawQuery: SELECT sid, sql_id, ROUND(elapsed_time/1000000, 2) as elapsed_seconds, sql_text FROM v$sql_monitor WHERE status = 'EXECUTING' AND elapsed_time/1000000 > 300 ORDER BY elapsed_time DESC FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY
